source.author: verg
source.text: Hic canit errantem lunam solisque labores; unde hominum genus et pecudes; unde imber et ignes; Arcturum pluviasque Hyadas geminosque Triones; quid tantum Oceano properent se tinguere soles hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
source.text_original: Hic canit errantem lunam solisque labores; / unde hominum genus et pecudes; unde imber et ignes; / Arcturum pluviasque Hyadas geminosque Triones; / quid tantum Oceano properent se tinguere soles / hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
source.text_english: Here he sings of the wandering moon and the labors of the sun; whence the race of men and cattle; whence rain and fire; Arcturus and the rainy Hyades and the twin Triones; why the winter suns make such haste to dip themselves in Ocean, or what delay hinders the slow nights.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quid tantum Oceano properent se tingere soles Hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
reuse.text_original: Quid tantum Oceano properent se tingere soles Hiberni, vel quae tardis mora noctibus obstet.
reuse.text_english: Why do the western suns hasten so much to dip themselves in Ocean, or what delay holds back the slow nights?
